record.title: Cybersecurity Standard Practice Guide — Guide to Security Emergency Response for Generative Artificial Intelligence Services
record.original_title: 网络安全标准实践指南——生成式人工智能服务安全应急响应指南
record.issuing_body: National Cybersecurity Standardization Technical Committee (TC260) Secretariat
record.summary: TC260 practice guide that implements the Interim Measures for generative AI services by giving providers a method to classify and grade generative AI service security incidents and an emergency response process. Incidents are information content, data security, cyberattack or other incidents, graded from level 1 (especially major) to level 4 (general). The process covers preparation (response team, plans, keyword and test-question banks, drills), monitoring (a refusal rate of at least 95% on the should-refuse test bank for hot events), handling, with service restriction or takedown and reporting of serious incidents to the competent department, and review.
record.notes: Version V1.0-202509, released with notice 网安秘字〔2025〕125号 dated 15 Sept 2025 and posted on 22 Sept 2025. A generative AI service security incident is defined as an event caused by human factors, malicious attacks or inherent model flaws that damages the service or its data and has negative effects on the state, society or economy. Classification and grading follow GB/T 20986-2023, and illegal and unhealthy information mainly means the 29 risks in Annex A (A.1 to A.4) of GB/T 45654-2025 (CN-10). Self-assessed incidents of level 3 or higher with possible wide public impact are to be reported to the competent department immediately when they occur five times within 24 hours, affect more than 10,000 users and may cause adverse social impact; general incidents are handled internally and reported periodically. Annex A gives cases of a discrimination incident and a false-information incident.

verification.note: Stored from tc260.org.cn: the guide's PDF (version V1.0-202509) and the release notice 网安秘字〔2025〕125号 (HTML, rendered copy and print). Title, number, issuer, date and contents are confirmed from these; the summary follows the Chinese text. No English version was found. A China Law & Practice page on the guide is stored (secondary); it is a subscription law digest whose content is not visible, so it is not recorded as an English version. It gives the issue date as 15 September 2025, matching the notice's signature date.

judgment.status_reasoning: The TC260 Secretariat released the guide with notice 网安秘字〔2025〕125号 (关于发布 ... 的通知, a release notice, not a call for comments); the cover carries the guide's number and a released version (V1.0-202509) with no draft marking (征求意见稿). The preface describes practice guides as technical documents the TC260 Secretariat drafts and publishes to give practical guidance, so it is not binding; no later version is stored. Published (non-binding, current).
judgment.date_reasoning: The notice is dated 2025-09-15; it was posted on the TC260 site on 2025-09-22. The signature date is used as the issue date.
judgment.scope_reasoning: AI-specific security guidance from TC260, the national cybersecurity standardisation committee: a government safety and risk-management guideline (AGENTS.md section 10, in with no note).
judgment.instrument_type_reasoning: TC260 practice guides are 'standard-related technical documents' giving practical guidance, not national standards; recorded as Guidelines / framework.
